items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear, but the code was not gofmt'd: batch.go has misaligned `commitJobID          int` / `commitCorrelationID uint64`, and event.go has a double blank line. A large goroutine closure inside commitWrite has no comments, and the public methods have only one-line docs.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Putting durabilityManager in its own file is good. However, writeWALRecord is a nested closure that spawns a goroutine inside commitWrite, outside the commit pipeline. The wait loops in WaitForDurabilityContext and WaitForJobDurabilityContext are near-duplicates. `b.applyDuration` is never set (dead field).

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: applyInternal calls d.newJobID() without holding d.mu, a data race on d.mu.nextJobID. ApplyDuration is never measured; it is faked as `applyDuration = 1 * time.Nanosecond`. SeqNum is the batch's first seq, not its last. Job retention breaks with the shared job ID space (the hidden expired/unknown test fails).

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: Every sync commit (including NoSyncWait) now spawns a goroutine, allocates a WaitGroup and takes a manager mutex, even when BatchDurable is unset. It also uses the DB's shared nextJobID counter (unlocked), which shifts the JobIDs reported by existing flush/compaction events.
